memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You shall not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not hold
anyone guiltless who misuses his name.'" - Ex 20:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
We usually reduce this to swearing. That is included, but it is much smaller than
what the command covers.

To misuse God's name is to attach it to something empty. It means invoking God
carelessly, using His name to add weight to our own agenda, promising in His name
what we do not intend to keep, or claiming He has spoken when He has not.

That last one is worth pausing on. Saying "God told me" about our own preference
is a serious use of His name. So is claiming His endorsement for our politics,
our decisions, or our treatment of someone we dislike.

There is a quieter form too. To be called by His name and live carelessly is to
misrepresent Him. Every Christian carries His name. Paul quotes Isaiah's rebuke:
"God's name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you" (Rom 2:24).

Jesus taught us to pray "hallowed be your name" (Matt 6:9) before anything else,
before daily bread or forgiveness. The honouring of God's name comes first.

His name is not a tool. It is who He is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever claimed God's backing for something that was really your own
   preference?
2. Does your life honour or cheapen the name you carry?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, hallowed be Your name. Keep me from using it carelessly or attaching it
to my own agenda. Amen.
